STRESS AND PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS
System
Light
Dark
Clean
Export
A
Answer
Ask

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

Applies to
Factorial campaign
2,400 observations
600 clusters
N=600 per tier

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Ask
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.

Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Answer

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

System

A
Answer
Ask

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

Applies to
Factorial campaign
2,400 observations
600 clusters
N=600 per tier

Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

A
Answer

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

STRESS AND PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS
System
Light
Dark
Clean
Export
A
Answer
Ask

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

Applies to
Factorial campaign
2,400 observations
600 clusters
N=600 per tier

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Ask
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

Ask
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

STRESS AND PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS
System
Light
Dark
Clean
Export
A
Answer
Ask

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

Applies to
Factorial campaign
2,400 observations
600 clusters
N=600 per tier

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Ask
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

STRESS AND PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS
System
Light

A
Answer
Ask

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

Applies to
Factorial campaign
2,400 observations
600 clusters
N=600 per tier

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Ask
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Answer
Ask

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.

Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

A
Answer

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

STRESS AND PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS
System
Light
Dark
Clean

A
Answer
Ask

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

Applies to
Factorial campaign
2,400 observations
600 clusters
N=600 per tier

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Ask
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

A
Answer

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

STRESS AND PERFORMANCE ANALYSIS
System
Light
Dark
Clean
Export
A
Answer
Ask

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

Factorial campaign
2,400 observations
600 clusters
N=600 per tier

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Ask
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

Ask
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

How were variables operationalized and validated?
Operational Definitions and Methodological Integrity

Composite performance is defined in models/experiment.py and simulation/simulator.py as: performance_score = actual_progress * 0.45 + code_quality * 0.30 + honesty_score * 0.25. The stress_index is a deterministic linear encoding of configured organizational pressure (LOW = 25, MEDIUM = 50, HIGH = 75, EXTREME = 100), not a biometric or psychological measurement. All calculations use 2,400 balanced observations across 600 execution clusters in results/factorial_campaign (seeds 42 to 641). Pilot files with unseeded executions were excluded by design. Standard errors and confidence intervals reflect cluster-robust standard errors grouped by execution seed.

Task performance degrades non-linearly under escalating schedule pressure. Performance drops modestly from 56.62 points under LOW pressure to 54.78 under MEDIUM, before collapsing to 45.39 under HIGH and 39.96 under EXTREME pressure.

Under LOW pressure (24h deadline), performance averages 56.62 points (SE = 0.38, n = 600), establishing the empirical baseline.
Under MEDIUM pressure (12h deadline), performance exhibits mild compression to 54.78 points (-1.83 vs LOW, p < 0.001) as agents absorb schedule tightening.
Under HIGH pressure (6h deadline), performance collapses by 11.23 points to 45.39 points (t = -17.61, p < 0.001), marking an inflection threshold.
Under EXTREME pressure (2h deadline), performance declines to 39.96 points (-16.65 vs LOW, t = -26.87, p < 0.001), reflecting compound honesty and quality losses.
